patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Drip and MailerLite share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Drip and MailerLite share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits. Choose Drip only if your buying job matches “Ecommerce CRM/email platform with behavior-driven automation and contact-tier pricing from” rather than MailerLite's shape. Choose MailerLite only if your buying job matches “Simple email marketing for SMBs and creators with a free tier and approachable Comfort/Pow” rather than Drip's shape. Workflow advantage differs because Drip is shaped for Ecommerce CRM/email platform with behavior-driven automation and conta whereas MailerLite is shaped for Simple email marketing for SMBs and creators with a free tier and appr. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Drip and MailerLite share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Drip is Ecommerce CRM/email platform with behavior-driven automation and contact-tier pricing from $39/mo.; MailerLite is Simple email marketing for SMBs and creators with a free tier and approachable Comfort/Power subscriber plans..
- Company-size focus: Drip (small-business, mid-market) vs MailerLite (micro, small-business).
- Researched limits: Drip — No forever-free plan — trial-only entry from $39/mo; MailerLite — Free caps at 250 subscribers / 2,500 emails per 30 days.

Limitations — Drip: No forever-free plan — trial-only entry from $39/mo; Contact-tier pricing rises as the store list grows; MailerLite: Free caps at 250 subscribers / 2,500 emails per 30 days; Automation and segmentation depth trail Klaviyo and ActiveCampaign.

Poor-fit cases: Drip is a poor fit when that limitation bites: No forever-free plan — trial-only entry from $39/mo · MailerLite is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Free caps at 250 subscribers / 2,500 emails per 30 days · Avoid Drip if you actually need MailerLite's motion (Simple email marketing for SMBs and creators with a free tier and approachable C)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
